If you plan to study MBBS in China in 2027, start with three checks: the university's latest admission status, the full six-year cost and the medical licensing rules in the country where you want to practise.

Selected Chinese universities offer English-medium Clinical Medicine programmes for international students. Current published tuition at the universities compared below ranges from about RMB 34,000 to RMB 75,000 per year.

The cheapest offer is not always the best one.

China's Ministry of Education states that undergraduate medical education in English for international students runs for six years and that the English degree title is MBBS. Chinese language is also compulsory during the programme because students need it for study, daily life and clinical contact with patients. 

If you are still deciding where to study medicine, it is worth comparing China with other medical-study destinations before committing to a six-year programme.

Nanjing's latest MBBS notice confirms six years including a one-year internship, English-medium teaching, RMB 34,000 annual tuition and CSCA Mathematics and Chemistry. 

Jilin lists MBBS as one of its English-taught undergraduate programmes, with six years of study, RMB 36,000 annual tuition and a 30 June 2026 deadline. 

Zhejiang's 2026 programme list gives Clinical Medicine (MBBS) a six-year duration, tuition of RMB 42,800 per year and a 31 May deadline. It also requires Mathematics and Chemistry for CSCA. 

Fudan's latest MBBS programme runs for six years at RMB 75,000 per year. Its 2026 admissions process required CSCA Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry followed by an interview. 

Jiangsu University currently lists six years, English-medium teaching, RMB 34,000 annual tuition, CSCA Mathematics and Chemistry, and an autumn 2026 deadline of 30 June. 

The point of the tracker is not to declare one university "best". It is to help you compare current facts before the 2027 notices arrive.

MBBS in China Fees for International Students

For students comparing fees for MBBS in China, tuition is only the first number.

A realistic budget also includes accommodation, insurance, medical examinations, residence-related charges, books, food, transport and travel.

Latest MBBS Tuition Fees in China for International Students

The verified examples above show a wide range:

  • Nanjing Medical University: RMB 34,000/year
  • Jiangsu University: RMB 34,000/year
  • Zhengzhou University: RMB 35,000/year
  • Jilin University: RMB 36,000/year
  • Dalian Medical University: RMB 42,000/year
  • Zhejiang University: RMB 42,800/year
  • Fudan University: RMB 75,000/year

Zhengzhou University's current fee structure also lists on-campus accommodation at RMB 5,000 or RMB 10,000 per year, insurance at RMB 1,000 per year and estimated living expenses of around RMB 600 to 1,000 per month. 

Dalian Medical University lists MBBS tuition at RMB 42,000 per year and double-room accommodation at RMB 10,000 per year on its current undergraduate programme page.

A student at a mid-fee university may reasonably plan for roughly RMB 55,000 to 75,000 per year once normal tuition, basic accommodation, insurance and living expenses are combined. The actual cost of MBBS in China depends heavily on the university, city and lifestyle.

Here is the part students often miss. A RMB 5,000 annual difference becomes RMB 30,000 across six years.

A proper MBBS in China fee structure should therefore show the whole degree, not just first-year tuition.

MBBS in China 2027 Intake and Admission

Students starting their research now should focus mainly on the 2027 intake.

Current admission dates show how much university timelines can differ. Nanjing and Jilin used 30 June 2026 deadlines, Zhejiang used 31 May, while Fudan's two 2026 phases were much earlier, from 1 to 15 January and 23 February to 6 March.

A practical planning timeline is:

Do not assume every MBBS course in China follows one national deadline. Always check the official university website for the latest admission requirements, deadlines and procedures.

MBBS in China Requirements for International Students

MBBS in China requirements vary, but the main academic pattern is consistent.

Applicants normally need a high-school or equivalent qualification with strong science results, appropriate English ability, good health and evidence that they can finance their studies.

Academic Subjects

Biology and Chemistry are central to medical admission. Physics and Mathematics also appear in the entry criteria or assessments of several universities.

Nanjing's latest requirements, for example, expect high-school study in Physics or Mathematics, Biology and Chemistry.

English Requirements

Requirements differ by institution.

Nanjing accepts IELTS 6.0, TOEFL 85 or Duolingo 115 under its latest published criteria. Zhejiang lists IELTS 6.0 overall or TOEFL iBT 75, while Jiangsu University lists IELTS above 6.0, TOEFL above 80 or Duolingo above 100.

CSCA

The China Scholastic Competency Assessment (CSCA) has become a particularly important admission entity.

Nanjing, Jilin, Zhejiang, Jiangsu University, Fudan and Xi'an Jiaotong all reference CSCA in current undergraduate or MBBS admission material. The subjects vary by university and programme.

That is why a 2027 applicant should not rely on an old admission guide.

How to Apply for MBBS in China in 2027

If you are researching how to apply for MBBS in China, start one step earlier than most students do.

Decide where you want to practise medicine after graduation.

Then follow this order:

  1. Check the foreign-medical-graduate rules in your target country.
  2. Shortlist suitable English-medium Clinical Medicine programmes.
  3. Verify the latest university admission notice.
  4. Compare tuition, accommodation, teaching hospitals and internship structure.
  5. Check subject, English, CSCA and interview requirements.
  6. Prepare your passport, school certificate, transcripts, English evidence, medical examination and other requested documents.
  7. Submit the university application.
  8. Review the admission offer, payment terms and university policies.
  9. Complete student registration and university onboarding steps.
  10. Keep every transcript, internship record and official university document.

That sequence makes MBBS admission in China much safer than choosing a university first and checking licensing requirements later.

Students applying specifically from Bangladesh can also explore the wider process for planning university study in China from Bangladesh. For MBBS applicants, this article provides a focused overview of the medical admission pathway, while the linked guide covers broader study options in China.

Documents Commonly Required

Typical documents include a passport, high-school certificate, transcripts, English-language evidence, medical examination report, financial evidence, personal statement and non-criminal record where required.

Several current programmes also ask for a CSCA transcript. Some add recommendation letters or interviews.

If you are preparing health paperwork, the practical requirements are covered separately in this guide to medical documentation for overseas study.

How Long Is MBBS in China?

MBBS in China normally takes six years.

The Ministry of Education's English-medium medical education standard specifies six years. Xi'an Jiaotong, Nanjing, Jilin, Zhejiang and Fudan also publish six-year MBBS or Clinical Medicine programmes in their current information.

The programme normally combines basic medical sciences, clinical subjects, hospital rotations and internship.

At Xi'an Jiaotong, for example, the six-year structure includes Chinese language and terminology, basic medical courses, clinical courses and a final hospital internship.

If you are comparing an MBBS degree in China with other medical qualifications, it may help to understand how MBBS and MD differ across education systems.

Is MBBS in China Taught in English?

Yes. International students can study medicine in China through eligible English-medium MBBS or Clinical Medicine programmes.

But English-medium does not mean Chinese is optional.

China's Ministry of Education requires Chinese language throughout the undergraduate medical programme, partly because students need to communicate with patients during clinical training.

Jiangsu University also currently requires HSK 4 with a score of at least 180 for graduation from its English-medium Clinical Medicine programme.

Think about it this way. You may understand an English pathology lecture perfectly and still struggle during a ward round if you cannot speak with the patient.

That is why teaching language and clinical language are two separate checks.

MOE, WDOMS and Medical Recognition

"Recognised worldwide" sounds reassuring. It is also too vague to base a medical career on.

The Ministry of Education regulates the Chinese side of English-medium undergraduate medical education. Your right to practise after graduation depends on the regulator in the country where you want to work.

A listing in the World Directory of Medical Schools (WDOMS) does not automatically mean recognition, accreditation or endorsement by WDOMS, WFME or FAIMER. Read WDOMS's explanation of what a listing means

For students targeting the United States, the ECFMG Sponsor Note matters. ECFMG states that if a school's World Directory listing does not include the appropriate Sponsor Note, its students and graduates are not eligible for ECFMG Certification. ECFMG also explicitly says that it does not recognise, accredit or endorse medical schools. Check ECFMG guidance on Sponsor Notes

For the UK, the General Medical Council assesses whether an overseas primary medical qualification is acceptable before PLAB or registration. See the GMC's overseas qualification guidance

The practical rule is simple.

Check licensing before admission, not after graduation.

Scholarships for MBBS in China

Scholarships can reduce MBBS fees in China, but the amount and conditions vary sharply.

Its scholarship availability depends on the category and available places.

Fudan's 2026 MBBS guide states that two outstanding admitted applicants can receive a Shanghai Government Scholarship Class B with tuition exemption.

So do not stop at the phrase "scholarship available". Check the amount, number of awards, renewal conditions and whether it covers only tuition or other costs as well.

Is Studying MBBS in China Worth It in 2027?

For the right student, yes.

Studying MBBS in China can make sense if you want a six-year medical programme, can fund the entire course, are prepared to learn Chinese for clinical communication and have already checked your future licensing route.

It becomes a weaker choice when the decision depends only on cheap tuition or an agent's claim that a university is "globally recognised".

The mildly surprising part is that the cheapest university can become the most expensive choice if the programme creates problems with internship records, clinical requirements or medical registration later.

You should also weigh the practical advantages and disadvantages of studying abroad before committing to six years overseas.

FAQs About MBBS in China

What are the fees for MBBS in China?

Current official examples checked for this guide range from about RMB 34,000 per year at Nanjing Medical University and Jiangsu University to RMB 75,000 per year at Fudan University. These are current planning figures, not confirmed 2027 fees.

What is the cost of MBBS in China for six years?

Tuition alone is approximately RMB 204,000 at Nanjing or Jiangsu University, RMB 216,000 at Jilin, RMB 256,800 at Zhejiang and RMB 450,000 at Fudan. Living expenses, accommodation, insurance, travel and other costs are extra.

How long is MBBS in China?

English-medium MBBS in China normally takes six years, including academic and clinical training.

What are the MBBS in China requirements?

Students generally need a high-school qualification with strong science results, appropriate English proficiency, good health and sufficient finances. Many current programmes also require CSCA results, while some use interviews.

Can international students study MBBS in China in English?

Yes. Selected universities offer English-medium Clinical Medicine programmes for international students. Chinese remains important because clinical training involves Chinese-speaking patients.

Is MBBS in China recognised worldwide?

No medical degree gives automatic practice rights in every country. Check the university and programme, then verify the rules of the medical regulator where you intend to practise.

Is the MBBS in China 2027 intake open?

It depends on the university. As of 20 August 2026, the universities checked for this guide are mainly publishing 2026 or 2026-2027 information. Students should use those figures for planning and confirm the new 2027 notice before applying.

Can I get a scholarship for MBBS in China?

Yes, some universities offer entrance or tuition scholarships. Nanjing currently lists awards from RMB 5,000 up to full tuition, while Fudan lists limited tuition-exemption opportunities for outstanding admitted applicants.

Before You Apply

If you want to study MBBS in China in 2027, work backwards from your future medical registration.

Check the regulator first. Then compare university status, tuition, admission requirements, teaching hospitals and internship arrangements.

If you need help narrowing the shortlist, you can discuss your academic profile, budget and intended intake with an adviser.

Do not start by asking which university is cheapest.

Start by asking which programme you can verify.
